text.p: Colombian insurance giant Compania Suramericana de Seguros said Thursday it was looking to make investments in insurance firms in Venezuela, Panama and the Dominican Republic this year.
The firm, the flagship of the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, also said it would be making substantial investments in electricity generation and gas pipelines in Colombia.

Suramericana did not say how much it would invest in the foreign insurance companies. It currently has stakes in Seguros America de Nicaragua, Argentina's Caja ART, Peru's Positiva and Profutura, Bolivia's Alianza, Equivida in Ecuador and Reasuguradora Nuevo Mundo of Panama.

This year Suramericana is planning to invest $80 million in Merilectrica, which is building a 160 megawatt thermo-electric generating plant due to come on stream in November. It will also pump $74 million into Transmetano, which is building a 100 mile (150 km) gas pipeline.
Suramericana said it hoped to tie up trade deals with Mavesa, HJ Heinz, Maizoro and Molinos de Rio Plata over the year but did not specify what the proposed ventures would entail.

Last year Suramericana and its subsidiaries Suramericana de Seguros de Vida, Suramericana de Capitalizacion and Administradora Suramericana de Inversiones reported net profits of $119.7 million in 1996 down from $139.8 million in 1995.
